record.summary: Amends the Criminal Code Act 1995 so that transmitting sexual material of an adult without consent is an offence carrying up to six years' imprisonment, whether the material is unaltered or created or altered using technology, including AI-generated deepfakes. It adds aggravated offences (seven years) for repeat offenders after three or more civil penalty orders under the Online Safety Act 2021 and for those who created or altered the material, with double-jeopardy and alternative-verdict rules.
record.notes: Assented to on 2 September 2024; the whole Act commenced on 3 September 2024, the day after Royal Assent. The Government's response to the Senate Select Committee on Adopting AI (April 2026) cites these August 2024 Criminal Code amendments on AI-generated sexual material.
record.scope_note: Not an AI-specific law: it amends the Criminal Code offence on sharing sexual material without consent and states that this covers material created or altered with AI (deepfakes). Included as the operative Australian criminal law on sexual deepfakes.
